_readme: One entry per company. The SUBJECT is one of them, named by `subject` below.
Every company must be the SAME reporting basis, downloaded from the same Screener
view. peer_ingest.py reads the basis out of each export header and hard-errors on a
mismatch, so a standalone file slipped into a consolidated set cannot get through.
`price` is the close on the report's cover date. Supply it for every company or the
comps are struck on different days. If omitted, the export's own price block is used
`surplus_investments` is the ONLY part of Screener's 'Investments' line netted from
EV. Leave it null unless the annual report shows genuinely surplus liquid
investments; strategic and subsidiary holdings must not be netted. See
`forward` stays empty unless you have consensus estimates. Any number in it requires
`source` and `as_of`, and the result is reported separately from everything computed,
never blended into the trailing median.
`yahoo` is only needed when the ticker is not <TICKER>.NS — market_data.py assumes an
NSE listing. Use .BO for BSE-only names. Leave it out otherwise. If you are not using
market_data.py at all, ignore `yahoo` and fill in `price` by hand.
subject: EICHERMOT
